items.rationale: Necessary dismantling and refitting in the damaged basement is covered under §§5.2.6–5.2.7. The comparable service in Case 46 supports €90 for one service.
Section 5.2.7 covers drying for the period supported by moisture readings. Seven billed days fit within the reported drying period and are estimated at €313 gross.
Section 7.4.4 bars this unexplained surcharge without a material breakdown. If itemized and shown necessary, the comparable charge is €39.
Replacing insulation disturbed by necessary access is covered under §5.2.6 if it matches the original diameter and standard under §7.14(c). The comparable allowance is €26 for one piece.
Section 5.2.2 pays only the first charge for the same disposal, based on the volume actually generated. The drying contractor's first-listed charge is estimated at €60 for the basement debris.
Section 5.2.6 covers levelling needed to restore the affected wall. Case 46 supports €38 for this material line.

Section 5.2.6 covers necessary substrate preparation, but §§3.5(d) and 7.4.1 bar work already charged as levelling or skilled labour. If this is a distinct preparation step, 2.78 m² at about €28/m² gives €78.
Section 5.2.6 expressly covers a necessary service opening in the affected wall. The comparable single-opening charge in Case 46 supports €19.

The format is within §7.14(d), but §§3.5(a), 3.5(e) and 7.1.6 limit the allowance to standard-grade tiles and the quantity reasonably needed, including cuts. Case 46 supports about €165 gross for the comparable affected area.

These tiles exceed the 90 × 90 cm limit in §7.14(d), and §3.5(f) denies partial payment for an over-threshold item. The €165 conditional estimate is for a standard equivalent only, not an additional allowance on top of line 9.
Necessary finishing joints are covered under §5.2.6 at the standard sanitary silicone grade in §7.14(a). At about €13/m, the gross threshold is €47.
Section 7.4.2 allows the first travel charge for this contractor on this document. The near-identical Case 46 supports €83 gross.
Section 7.4.1 covers necessary hours at customary rates, excluding labour already included in other lines. The same-quantity prior puts the gross threshold at €1,239 if all 14 hours are supported.

items.description: Remove basement drywall and insulation wool
items.rationale: Sections 5.2.1 and 5.2.6 cover necessary removal in the damaged basement, but the flat rate needs the breakdown required by §7.4.4. If substantiated, comparable drywall and insulation work totals about €95, excluding any duplicate disposal.

Sections 5.2.1 and 7.1.5 cover removal of established water-damaged plaster in the basement, provided it is distinct from the other demolition. The stated prior supports €29 for the single billed unit.
Section 3.5(b) excludes work outside the documented damage area, and the claim identifies the attic work as unrelated. The €29 conditional estimate uses the single-unit plaster-removal benchmark.
Sections 5.2.2 and 3.5(d) exclude this second charge for the same disposal already listed at position 5. The €60 conditional benchmark would apply only to a payable disposal charge.
